summary: ORBITAL is an offline-first health monitoring app that helps astronauts assess their own health on long-duration missions. Crew members log daily indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, glucose, temperature, sleep, mood, stress, radiation dose and symptoms) manually, through a Bluetooth smartwatch, camera-based pulse or CSV import. ORBITAL compares each value with the astronaut’s own personal baseline as well as configurable ranges, and shows a clear color-coded status: normal, monitor or needs attention. An interactive 3D body map links each body system to spaceflight hazards, while alerts, recommendations, health tasks and a knowledge center explain what to do next. To handle communication delay with Earth, ORBITAL prepares one complete medical packet. Its architecture adds a digital twin on the ground that estimates the astronaut’s present state, so a flight surgeon can send back a signed if-then plan. This replaces four round trips with one and lets the astronaut act immediately. ORBITAL runs as a single self-contained HTML file. It is a decision-support prototype, not a diagnostic tool.
details:
What it does. ORBITAL gives astronauts a quick self-assessment of six health domains: cardiovascular, blood glucose, body temperature, sleep and recovery, psychological well-being, and radiation exposure. Each domain gets a color-coded status, a trend chart, an explanation and recommended actions.

How it works. Each indicator has configurable ranges and a personal baseline (rolling mean and standard deviation of up to 30 readings, excluding the latest 7 days). A deviation of 2 SD or more triggers “Monitor”, and 3.5 SD or more triggers “Needs attention”. Alert rules cover threshold crossings, baseline deviation, sustained drift, multi-stressor shifts, red-flag symptoms, radiation milestones and overdue checks. Data comes from manual entry, a Bluetooth heart-rate watch, camera pulse or CSV import. An interactive 3D body map, hazard pages, health tasks with streaks, and a knowledge center help astronauts who are not medical experts.

Earth link and digital twin. With a delay of up to 20 minutes each way, ORBITAL builds one complete medical packet that the astronaut chooses to share. On Earth, a digital twin (one Kalman filter per indicator) estimates the astronaut’s state now and when the reply will arrive. The doctor writes an if-then plan, tests it on 500 simulated futures and signs it. The board verifies the signature, expiry and dose limits before acting.

Impact. Astronauts can detect changes early, act without waiting for Earth, and need one round trip instead of four. The same idea applies to remote clinics on Earth.

Tools. React 18, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Three.js, Web Bluetooth, the Camera API, localStorage and Vite (single-file build, so it works offline).
Creativity and factors considered. Comparing each astronaut to their own normal, hiding latency instead of fighting it, privacy through consent levels, and honest limits.
Limits. All demo data is synthetic and labelled as such. Thresholds are illustrative, not flight medical limits. ORBITAL is not a diagnostic tool.
